posts.cooked:
xBlackWolfx:

I'll use insular primalis again (how are you supposed to pronounce that name anyway?).

I say it "inn-syoo-lah pry-mal-iss", personally.  I don't know if that's official or anything.

what is Absolute Zero good for anyway? He has to deal damage to himself to accomplish anything, and I mean anything, seriously the guy has to damage himself just to heal himself!

He heals instead of taking the damage, though.  He is a bit on the frustrating side, but also has potentially incredible output, if he jumps through all the proper hoops without interference.  Picture this setup:  At the start of his turn, Impale deals 2 damage to a target, which Focused Apertures increases to 3.  He then activates Thermal Shockwave to deal 1 cold damage to each of three targets; the Apertures increase that to 2 each.  So he's dealt a total of 9 cold damage this turn; Thermal Shockwave deals 9 fire damage to him, and Isothermic Transducer turns that into 10 cold damage thanks to the Apertures again.  He can either hit the same target as his Impale and one of the Shockwave hits, making a total of 14 damage that turn, or if he has both modules out, he can have the Transducer "damage" him, enabling him to regain all the HP he lost to the Shockwave and 1 more besides.  (Do note that if the Shockwave damage kills him first, he doesn't get the chance to heal.  This is why Cold Snap plus Shockwave is probably not a good idea, and Cold Snap plus Focused Apertures plus Shockwave is really not a good idea.)

He's heavily reliant on a few specific equipment cards, and buffs from other heroes or the environment.

The former at least is true, he does badly need at least one module to get anything done, and both to work ideally.  But he has four copies of each, plus four copies of the Installation card which searches them out (and lets you draw another card, and if you didn't need to play the Module you searched for you can play a different card instead, so you basically drew one new card without costing yourself anything, as well as trading the Installation for any Module in your deck - do try to count how many are left as you play, though, since you get nothing if they're all in your trash or if you draw the last one before searching).  Buffs from other heroes are not necessary, although they can be amazing - Embolden from Fanatic will let him fire a Coolant Blast after a Thermal Shockwave, dealing a second instance of cold damage equal to the fire damage you took, or it will let you pop Cryo-Chamber for 4 fire damage to yourself before Coolant Blasting for 4+ (although the two aren't normally a great combo; unless you played the Cryo-Chamber that same turn, it cost you a point of fire each time you got hit during the previous round).

Not to mention he pretty much can't do anything until you get set up, I mean seriously his innate power does nothing but damage him

This is why he is one of the heroes most likely to spend his first turn drawing 2 cards.  However he's hardly unique in this - Unity's power does nothing without an Equipment (her own or an ally's) that can be spared and a Golem to turn it into.  Nightmist takes damage to draw cards, which is a painful trade unless she has redirection out.  Argent Adept is useless without a song, Expatriette can do very little without a Gun, Mr. Fixer needs a Tool and a Style…very few characters are as good "out of the box" as Ra and Haka, most of them have to do a fair bit of legwork in order to get rolling, and can be undone badly by a wipe card such as TechSing or Flechettes (or Dawn's Devastating Aurora, which destroys ALL non-villain cards in play, except for Unity's golems or Visionary's Decoy Projection).

Not to mention other heroes (like Ra and Wraith) can easily match his damage output, without damaging themselves

Let me know how often Ra or Wraith can deal 29 damage to one target.  That's the theoretical maximum output of AZ's damage if he does everything exactly right, assuming no external boosts.  (Deal exactly 28 cold damage out including Thermal Shockwave, then Isometric Transducer dishes 29 out thanks to Focused Apertures.)  Fanatic is the only other character that can wallop that hard, and she also ends up at 1 HP afterward (as well as before), but she has only one copy of the triggering card, and must discard 3 cards to use it.

In actual practice, of course, Fanny is probably somewhat better than AZ across the board.  But both are self-damaging heroes, and both give you reasons to damage yourself.  If you can't get the hang of knowing when to let yourself get hurt and when not to, well, maybe these two aren't for you.  But they can definitely be good to have on your team.

and wraith has alot more versatility than Absolute Zero to boot.

Wraith has more versatility than anyone (except possibly Argent Adept, depending on who he's paired with).  If you made a list of the best heroes in the game, it's virtually certain Wraith would be in the top three no matter who was making the list, unless it was purely subjective.  She's a little boring once you "solve" her, but she's just ridiculously good.  Don't criticize other heroes for failing to be The Wraith; they each have their own little niches in which they can shine.

Was he designed to give players a challenge or something?

Among other things.  He's not a handicap, but he is designed to appeal to players who grow bored with the straightforwardness of Ra and Legacy, and want to jump through a few hoops and make themselves look/feel clever.  I'm one of those players, and AZ is in my top third of heroes in the game for precisely this reason…he feels like a puzzle that I enjoy solving.  Though I do think he might not be quite perfectly balanced, as compared to some of the other characters who have similar shticks but seem to execute them a little better (in particular, the other two 3-complexity heroes are both absurdly good when they get a dream setup, compared to which AZ is just okay).

and really the only advantages he does have are immunity to fire

I assume you're talking about using the Transducer to heal himself.  Note that becoming actually immune to fire damage (or to damage in general) is one of the worst things that can happen to him, as it turns off much of his ability to do anything.  This is in flavor for him, since Ryan Frost is a miserable old curmudgeon who does nothing but complain the whole time he's battling to save the world (another reason why I like him, having a similar personality much of the time).  In the words of Garbage, he's "Only Happy When It Rains".  (Tempest can help him with that.)

(sadly though, the villains don't seem to be big on dealing fire or cold damage, most of their damage cards do energy damage)

I agree that this is a little annoying.  Ra also wishes fire damage would get dealt more often, since he can make the entire party immune to it.  A fair number of Environments are fire-centric, but not as many as I'd like.  And I personally find energy damage to be quite unflavorful and unsatisfying (if it were up to me, I'd make most of it into lightning damage, occasionally fire or radiant - the latter type is almost exclusively found on Fanatic and occasionally on The Scholar, and seems to exist mostly as a way to make them feel more special than if they were dealing a "mere mortal" type of damage).

Is there any reason to every play AZ besides for a challenge?

Yes, every reason I stated above.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Focused Apertures in play.  3 cold damage from Impale (needs a target, but you almost certainly have at least one of those, unlike with ongoings and environments), 2 from Cold Snap, 3 from Hoarfire, which deals 3 fire damage to Zero, triggering Isothermic Transducer to deal 4 more cold, then Hoarfire goes on to deal 2 cold (this assumes you do NOT have NPCU in play) and 1 fire to Zero, triggering another 2 cold.  That's 3+2+3+4+2+2=16 outgoing cold damage, then 2 more from Shockwave on a single target, which is 18 outgoing cold damage, so 18 fire damage to Zero which triggers 19 more cold damage.

...Okay so it doesn't work exactly like I said, but it does mean you're dealing 35 cold damage to one target over the course of the turn, along with 22 to yourself.  That's even better than what I'd said before.  With even one other target, you get another 2 damage from Cold Snap and 2 more from Shockwave, resulting in 4 more fire damage to yourself and thus 4 more cold damage to the primary target.  You can't add a third Shockwave target without killing yourself, and if there are very many other targets at all, you probably want to replace Hoarfire with a card that won't damage you (Fueled Freeze is good if the number of targets is exactly right), and possibly ditch Cold Snap as well.

So even if I got the minutiae wrong, the point still stands: AZ can dish out more damage in an almost-complete vacuum than nearly any other hero, if he has exactly the right set of cards in play and is at sufficient health.  He even beats Wraith unless the target has reduction, though not by much.  And Ra isn't going to take much less damage than AZ keeping two Solar Flares in play long enough to play Flame Spike (especially with Staff of Ra and Imbued Fire already in play), whereas Wraith takes no damage but needs far more cards in play.  AZ looks pretty good in this particular bubble, even if it's fairly far from the typical conditions of actual play.

(Note that while I may have read about this trick in one of Flamethrower's guides originally, I am not consulting that guide as I type this; this is all from memory and looking at AZ's deck.)

BlackWolf, have you tried doing play-by-forum games?  I've only done one myself, but since you and I have such opposite views on Omnitron, I'd be willing to help you run a game against him and see if I can show you why I always have an easy time of it (or if you can show me why you don't).  I'm in US Central Time and tend to be free in the evenings, especially over the weekend (not Fridays though), so if we can arrange a time when we're both on, we could play such a game out in a few hours.  (Most of the online games take weeks of players making one move a day or so, but I lack the patience for that.)

xBlackWolfx:

omnitron was still at full health when everyone was at half

That sort of thing is not unusual for villains in general, though Omnitron is a bit less likely to get it than some others.  Most villains do tend to come out the gate guns blazing, and except for a few such as Tachyon, heroes nearly always have to build up a lot before they stabilize.  More than one game has ended with all the heroes down to about 5 HP; once they get all their stuff out, it's not hard to focus fire on the villain and bring him down by 10-20 HP each round.  If he pulls a Flechettes or TechSing at the wrong moment, it's trouble, but otherwise he's basically screwed.

I had a choice between destroying the explosive device (which was at 1) or take out a s-85 drone that was about to do 2 damage.

In most cases 2 damage to one hero is preferable to 1 damage on each of three heroes.  It depends on exactly what's in play, so it's not necessarily that you made the wrong call, but you might well have.

om pulled tech singularity (which I knew was going to happen), bc he was on his rampaging robot side, he drew another card, and it was a sedative.

Ouch.  Well, there's 2 of each card in a 25-card deck, so it's not statistically likely that he'll get that pairing, but it's definitely a wallop.  Perhaps you're just cursed with terrible luck?  Let's see if we can get your hands on Kismet's Talisman and do something about it. 

Fanatic didn't do anything at all, really all she did was sit there and ping stuff for like 1 and 2 damage.

Fanatic is a very hit-or-miss character.  I like to say that she's made for players who like to pray for a miracle; her cards are highly situational, but many of them are potential gamewinners.  Wrathful Retribution, End of Days, Divine Focus, Divine Sacrifice, Final Dive, Chastise, Smite the Transgressor, Sacrosanct Martyr, Zealous Offense - all extremely potent under very particular circumstances.  The rest of her cards are just sort of little plinks to bide time until "the clouds part" and you know exactly what you need to do.  Don't be afraid to have her spend a turn drawing two cards if damage reduction prevents her Exorcism from working.  She's largely there to tank with her high HP and bide her time, looking for an "I Win" button.

Visionary was only of mild help, she was useless when it came to combatting those explosives

You must not have drawn Wrest the Mind.  Did you have her Enlighten herself or play Foresight?  Conversely, she can also Enlighten a different character who might be stronger than her in a particular situation (Fanatic and Tempest could both have been good choices, depending on exactly what you had).

I actually had to chastise one (for two turns) just to keep my team alive.

Which was exactly the right thing to do in that case.

What I need is a team that can quickly deal 15 damage in a single turn to take care of those bombs.

Very hard to do with three characters (probably your best chance is either Ra + Absolute Zero +1 or Legacy + Fanatic + 1, where the other hero is either Haka, Tempest, or whichever of Legacy and Ra you aren't using.  But keep in mind, this team is built almost exclusively to do tons of damage, and will be in deep doo-doo if Omnitron sticks an Adaptive Plating after one or two heroes have died, because Tempest, Zero and Fanatic are the only ones of these characters who can remove ongoings, and only Fanatic and Tempest deal multiple damage types.

Are my problems having to do with the fact that I'm running three heroes instead of four?

Yes, or better yet five.  In a five player game, Legacy is absolutely bananas, and Omnitron is a punk.  Dealing 7 damage to kill a component or 15 to an EPE is trivial with that many heroes, and Omnitron has only a couple of H effects which are improved in such a game.  You've been fighting an uphill battle by using only 3.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Omnitron can be tricky, what with those bloody horrible Flechettes and Technological Singularities…and the EPEs of course. One game we had against him he played both EPEs in the same turn, if I remember rightly, or possibly played one on one turn and the second one on the following turn. Fortunately, however, Tachyon had two Hypersonic Assaults in-hand and was able to nerf both of them for long enough that we destroyed them before either was able to deal us any damage :D. Deck control can be very useful against Omnitron, though in terms of looking at what card he's going to play next you obviously can't always get full control on the turns in which he plays two cards. Stuff like Take Down or Mistbound can be good to more or less shut him down completely, though :).

If you had someone like Tempest or Ra (good damage/good AE stuff) teamed up with, say, Legacy (damage buffs), dealing with Omnitron and his bots might be a bit easier. You'd obviously have trouble if any stuff-destruction came out, though. I'm yet to try Omni-10 against Omnitron but I intend to do so at some point - Self-Sabotage lets you destroy ANY components, not just those belonging to Omni-10, hint hint ;). Of course, a Technological Singularity on Omnitron's part would be incredibly painful if it came out while Omni-10 was pretty well-equipped…but that's the risk, I suppose.

Wraith is another one who could be useful. Mind you, she's pretty good in any fight. She can control the deck with her Eyepiece, nerf damage with her Stun Bolts, deal it with her various throwable pointy things, and soak it with Stealth.

Unity might also be good, since her bots count as neither ongoings nor equipment, so would completely ignore either of the two stuff destruction cards. She can be pretty insane if she can get enough bots in play - paired with someone like the Adept or Omni-10 (who can help her get cards into play outside of her own turn, therefore she can put more bots out without needing to use her own powers) she can get set up that much faster, which is always nice :).

Regarding Omnitron and deck control…actually, regarding any character with the potential to draw two cards on their turn (eg Dawn, Spite, La Capitan) and deck control…it's fine being able to look at the top two cards of the villain deck and put one on top and one on the bottom (which is what most deck control things allow you to do), but that doesn't let you look at the second card said villain is going to play. You might reveal Truth and Spring from the top of Dawn's deck and put Truth on the bottom…but that won't save you from the Devastating Aurora which comes out after that Channel the Eclipse has brought out Spring at the start of the turn ;). Actually, this doesn't even solely apply to villains who have double-draw capabilities in their own decks - environments like Atlantis can let them get extra plays regardless.

There will also inevitably be occasions where the top two cards are both horrible, and in some cases, both the same. Then, some kind of trouble is unavoidable. Unless you've got a second source of deck control, I suppose, which can then look at that horrible top card and whatever the next card is, and maybe end up with a nicer card on top and both the horrible ones on the bottom. Or Omni-10, who can just Timeshift the horrible card into the trash :). If that's not an option, however, you'll just be sat there knowing what's going to happen on the villain's next turn, but being unable to do anything about it.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Any time anything deals damage and gives a number as its damage totals, each given number is a separate instance of damage - Fanatic's Exorcism is one example, of course - she deals one damage and one damage with her base power, therefore any damage boosts (or nerfs) will affect both those totals separately. Another example is Tempest's Vicious Cyclone, which says you can discard up to three cards and deal one damage for each card discarded. So if you are buffed with, say, Galvanise, you'd instead deal two damage for each card discarded.

It's the same with, say, the vats in Pike Industrial - the Supercooled trisolvent Vat deals something like one cold, one toxic, and erm, one something else at the end of the environment turn. If the erm…toxic vat (something-cyclohexane I think it's called…lol sorry bad memory this evening) is out, the one which converts all damage to toxic and increases it by one, the Trisolvent Vat will instead deal two toxic, two toxic, and two toxic damage at the end of the turn.

Compare to cards like Savage Mana, Omni-Cannon, and Lightspeed Barrage, which specify to "…deal X damage, where X is the number of cards…". So you'd total up the damage, and apply any buffs on top of that one total.

Apparently, my problem really was because I insisted on playing only 3 heroes.

I must be the only one who feels that 3 hero games are actually easier on average than 4. I play the majority of my solo games at H=3 with heros chosen at random. Deck manipulation becomes a much higher priority with 3. Visionary or Wraith should be focusing on Omnis deck to skirt the Explosives and fletches whenever possible.

I find that when I am having massive trouble with an encounter, adjusting your priorities is usually the quickest answer to success. By that I mean if you are giving priority to killing every single thing on the table before moving to omnitron, he will probably eventually get you as the game progresses. Obviously the Electro-Pulse should always be the highest priority target (either to crowd control through effects like Chastise or for nuking). But with Omnitron, most of the time hitting him and letting a bot or two live for a round or so is the best thing. Those components have to be destroyed, so every round there should be some damage going his way to keep cleared of those things.

Do not underestimate support abilities or effects that allow you to exert more control over the table. When I first got the game, I put way too much stock and emphisis on doing damage. Once I started shifting my card/effect priorities toward controling the tempo and flow of the game, things started getting much much easier. And in H=3 games, those same control effects become even more valuable. Damage Reduction for instance, is point by point more valuable in an H=3 game than H=4 or 5 as it becomes easier to totally negate instances of damage instead of just reducing them.

I guess I would sugest mixing up your play style a bit maybe. I understand some games the cards just arnt going to give you many options depending on the situation (and you should always play to the situation really), but try different things. I highly and strongly doubt the reason for your losses is just because you went H=3.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Bear in mind you can stop damage coming at you in other ways besides having soak on yourself - you can zap the bad guys with something that lowers their damage (Stun Bolt, for example), or redirect it with stuff like Synaptic Interruption or Driving Mantis, or do both in the case of Smoke Bombs.

Several characters can heal others - Tempest is pretty good at it (Cleansing Downpour), Omni-10 can heal multiple people (Innervation Ray, though only up to three if I remember rightly, so perhaps a little less useful in a game with more than three heroes), as can the Adept (Vernal Sonata/Rhapsody of Vigour, and he's also pretty good at healing himself with the right songs and instruments to combo).

I think Ab'Zero, Nightmist, and the Scholar are probably the three characters with the best means of healing themselves, but other characters such as Fanatic, Ra, Wraith, and Bunker can heal themselves to a certain degree (albeit not necessarily to a very reliable level, and often there's something you want to do more than healing yourself at any given moment).

Bunker can be a reasonable tank if he uses Heavy Plating and Recharge Mode. Legacy has been mentioned. The Scholar can have good soak via Flesh to Iron, and can use Alchemical Redirection to divert all damage to him for a round (alternatively he can use erm...that card which reduces all damage he receives to zero for a round), plus of course he's got plenty of ways to heal himself. In a way, Nightmist and Visionary both have means of tanking via their invincibility cards (Mistform and TK Cocoon, respectively), if they happen to be the highest/lowest hp in a situation where most of the damage is being aimed at them. Of course, this basically shuts them down from being able to do much else othe than draw, but it's something :). Omni-10 can tank a bit as well, now I think of it, if all incoming damage is of the "right" type(s) for whatever plating he happens to have out at the time, and is low enough not to break his components (and even if it does, he still gets to keep the plating) - had a good game versus the Matriarch a couple of weeks ago, whre Omni-10 had his Ablative Coating out, and Bunker his Heavy Plating and the highest hp. Wraith was the third hero and had taken quite a bit of bird damage so had the lowest hp - after a while she managed to get out Smoke Bombs, which meant any damage being dealt to her by Lilian was being redirected to Bunker, who soaked it. So Wraith wasn't getting hit at all, and Bunker and Omni-10 were both soaking all incoming villain damage. Yeah, Lilian didn't do too well that game (plus irreducible plasma cannon damage on Muninn = lol >:)).

Only hero that looks like he could actually tank at all (to me anyway) is legacy

The Scholar is ridiculously good at tanking…he can't lose HP fast enough with all the healing he does, usually he wants to get hurt so that he can heal and thus deal damage with Mortal Form To Energy.  Legacy is probably second to that, although he has the advantage that his "take damage for everyone" card doesn't go away after one round.  Haka is also a good tank, and Fanatic is adequate at it, as she can mega-nuke something when low on HP and has the Aegis to resurrect her if she gets abruptly killed.  Bunker is not as good at tanking as he should be, given that he's literally a tank (with arms and legs instead of wheels, but still, what else do you call an armored combat vehicle with a pilot inside), and AZ probably falls next in the order, though Nightmist is arguably better at the "I hurt myself except actually I don't" shtick (as opposed to Fanatic, who actually does hurt hurself in every case).

he has by far the best damage reduction in the game (danger sense and next evolution most notably)

Danger Sense only works on the Environment, which is relevant a lot less often than I'd like; I usually don't have a spare play to get it out.  Next Evolution can be great (especially in a Cyclohexane Vat heheh), but it's very frequently not as helpful as Galvanize or Motivational Charge, and you need a Legacy Ring to do both (conversely, without either Next Evolution or Motivational Charge, the Legacy Ring is useless, unless you're fighting in the Tomb of Anubis and can pick up a Relic…hm, I'll have to try that sometime).  Although the Ring is the exact same card as Wraith's Utility Belt, it proves far less useful due to the other cards in your deck; only those two (unless I'm forgetting one) have Powers, and neither is very often going to be preferable to Galvanize, nor is NE usually preferable to the other one if you are giving up Galvanize (or have the Ring).

and he has the ability to redirect damage to him, something taht to my knowledge the other heroes can't do (or at least, not as well as he can).

No, he's definitely unequaled in that regard.  But you don't need to be able to redirect damage in order to tank; just being highest (or lowest) HP and staying there is enough, as it means attacks will consistently be aimed at you (except when they hit everybody of course).

I might be doing something wrong though, since to me the heroes seem to be severely lacking in the defense department. At best, some can reduce all the damage to them by 1, and that's it (bc the cards that give them this have limited).

Bunker reduces damage by 2 when he's in Recharge Mode with Heavy Plating out.  But you're doing it right - 1 point of armor is usually the most a hero gets, and that's enough to make a significant difference.

I also find healing to be rather pathetic, I mean really the only two heroes that can heal more than 2 hit points are wraith (with a one-shot) and AZ (and only himself).

Again, you haven't seen Scholar, and also Argent Adept.  But you're right that the healing tends to be a bit lacking.  Tempest is the best healer in the EE; the 2 HP he restores each round is enough to keep ahead of some of the less violent villains, but it's often less advisable than Squalling everything (unless of course the enemy has out DR, as with advanced Omnitron on his Rampaging Robot side).

Well now that I think of it, haka can also heal for a lot, and reduce damage to himself, but he needs to discard ALOT of cards in order to accomplish this, and even then it would only be for one turn.

Do note that the card "Dominion" is not Limited.  Having multiples of those out and destroying Environment cards is the single best way to get the kind of card supply necessary to make full use of the Haka cards.  It's also fun to have Visionary in the game feeding you with Enlighten every turn.
